sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the north-eastern corner of Barrington between 2nd Avenue on the left and Barrington Avenue on the right, from Austin Avenue at the top south to Haines Avenue, drawn at the larger scale of 50 feet to an inch. Albany, Kingston and Reading Avenues cross the sheet, and Clement Bridge Road, also lettered Highland Avenue, runs diagonally through the bottom blocks towards the railroad. Beyond Barrington Avenue the Atlantic City Railroad (Philadelphia and Reading Railway) runs up the right side of the sheet along the boundary of the Borough of Haddon Heights, with the station on its east side next to Atlantic Avenue and a freight house on its west side; the area further east is left blank with a reference to the map of Haddon Heights, and a branch of Timber Creek crosses the upper right corner near a pump house. The blocks north of Reading Avenue are residential, with frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories, sheds and garages, and the J. M. Heake shirtwaist factory (power and lights electric, heated by hot air) on Barrington Avenue between Albany and Kingston Avenues. A private hospital stands on Reading Avenue near 2nd Avenue. The blocks along Clement Bridge Road form the small business centre, with stores, a post office, a bank at Barrington Avenue and Reading Avenue, a storage building, a cinder block store and buildings of brick and concrete block. Austin Avenue is marked not opened at the top. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes and hydrants are marked along the streets.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch; the other street sheets of the atlas are at 100 feet.
Clement Bridge Road is Clements Bridge Road in OpenStreetMap; Atlantic Avenue east of the railroad is East Atlantic Avenue.
The railroad is lettered A.C.R.R. (P. & R. R'y).
The right margin reads 'See Map of Haddon Heights'.

50 ft to an inch. 2nd Avenue to Barrington Avenue and the Atlantic City Railroad, Austin to Haines Avenue; shirtwaist factory, station, business blocks on Clement Bridge Road. One part. Barrington Avenue has no parcel width (railroad beside it): street_widths 60.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the northern residential grid of Barrington, from the North Branch of Timber Creek, which forms the boundary with the Borough of Haddon Heights along the top of the sheet, south to Trenton Avenue. Austin, Albany, Kingston, Reading and Haines Avenues cross the sheet from side to side, and 4th, 3rd and 2nd Avenues run down it; the 2nd Avenue frontage on the right edge continues on sheet 2. In the lower left corner the grid gives way to Lawrence Avenue and Moore Avenue, which run diagonally towards the south-west, with a strip of narrow lots between them and the Borough Play Ground beside Lawrence Avenue; this corner continues on sheet 5. Clement Bridge Road, also lettered Highland Avenue, crosses the lower right corner towards sheet 4. The blocks, numbered 13 to 30 and 39, are laid out in long narrow lots and built up mainly with frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories, with sheds and garages behind, and many lots are still empty, especially in the north-west. Larger buildings include the Public School on Haines Avenue at 3rd Avenue (heated by hot air, lit by electricity), a hall on Kingston Avenue near 2nd Avenue, a bakery at Reading Avenue and 2nd Avenue, a metal work shop on Kingston Avenue, a car shop, and a fire house with a fire ring and siren near Haines Avenue and 2nd Avenue. A few dwellings are of concrete block. Six-inch water pipes run along most streets, with hydrants marked. Two short streets at the top right are marked not open. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that the street grid is square to the page.
notes: Clement Bridge Road (printed 'Clement Bridge Rd. or Highland Av.') is Clements Bridge Road in OpenStreetMap.
The top margin reads 'See Map of Haddon Heights'.
100 ft. Pilot. North grid: Austin to Trenton Avenue, 4th to 2nd Avenue, Lawrence and Moore Avenues; public school. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre and south-east of Barrington, from Haines Avenue at the top south to Gloucester Pike and the open land beyond, and from the Lawrence Avenue and Moore Avenue blocks on the left to Barrington Avenue and the railroad on the right edge, where a line marks the boundary between the Borough of Barrington and the Borough of Lawnside. Clement Bridge Road, also lettered Highland Avenue, crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left towards the station, with Trenton Avenue, 3rd Avenue and 2nd Avenue meeting it near the top. Between Clement Bridge Road and Gloucester Pike, Newton Avenue and Woodland Avenue run south-east through a new subdivision of narrow lots, partly built with frame dwellings. East of 2nd Avenue, Erie Avenue and Ashland Avenue end short of Barrington Avenue and are marked not open beyond; Barrington Avenue south of Trenton Avenue is also marked not open. The sheet shows mostly frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories, with sheds and garages. Notable buildings are the 1st Presbyterian Church on Lawrence Avenue at Clement Bridge Road (heated by hot water, lit by electricity) and the First M. E. Church with its parsonage on Clement Bridge Road near Haines Avenue (heated by steam, lit by electricity). The large lower right part of the sheet, block 50, is open land with a single farmstead of dwellings, sheds, a corn crib, a spring house and storage buildings. The lower left corner continues on sheet 5 and the top edge on sheets 2 and 3. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Gloucester Pike is East Gloucester Pike in OpenStreetMap; Clement Bridge Road is Clements Bridge Road.
Lawrence Avenue meets Clement Bridge Road with a short jog and continues beyond it as Newton Avenue; the two junctions were left out of the control for that reason.
Erie Avenue and Ashland Avenue are marked not open towards Barrington Avenue; the modern 2nd Avenue extension to Ashland Avenue is not drawn.

100 ft. Haines to Gloucester Pike, Lawrence/Moore to Barrington Avenue; Newton and Woodland Avenues, Presbyterian and M.E. churches; farm in block 50. One part. Clement Bridge Road / Lawrence and Newton (jog) excluded.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the western side of Barrington around the junction of Clement Bridge Road and Gloucester Pike. Clement Bridge Road, also lettered Highland Avenue, crosses the sheet from the lower left towards the upper right, and Gloucester Pike runs from the top of the sheet south-east to meet it beside the public school. In the upper right corner Moore Avenue and Trenton Avenue enclose block 40, a group of small lots with frame dwellings that continues the Moore Avenue blocks of sheets 3 and 4; a filling station with gasoline tanks stands at its corner on Clement Bridge Road. Williams Avenue and Shreve Avenue run south from Clement Bridge Road through blocks 45 and 46 towards sheet 6, divided into long lots with only a few dwellings, sheds and a green house. The rest of the sheet is mostly open land: block 43 in the upper left is crossed by an unnamed road labelled only Road, with a farmstead of dwellings, barns, a pig pen, corn cribs and a windmill tower at its western end, and block 44 between the road and Clement Bridge Road holds scattered dwellings. The public school on Gloucester Pike is drawn as a brick building. Six-inch water pipes run along Gloucester Pike and Clement Bridge Road. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, turned about eight degrees further than the neighbouring sheets 3 and 4 so that Clement Bridge Road and the Williams Avenue lots are square to the page.
notes: Clement Bridge Road is Clements Bridge Road in OpenStreetMap; Gloucester Pike is East and West Gloucester Pike either side of it; Williams Avenue is East Williams Avenue.
The road crossing block 43 is lettered only 'Road'; it was not identified with a modern street and not used for control.
The fitted rotation (about 42 degrees) differs from sheets 3 and 4 (about 35 degrees); the drawn streets confirm the sheet is turned differently.
Only four street junctions were detected; a hand-picked point at Clement Bridge Road and Gloucester Pike disagreed by 5.5 m and was left out.
100 ft, turned about 8 degrees more than sheets 3 and 4. Clement Bridge Road and Gloucester Pike, Williams and Shreve Avenues, public school; mostly open land. One part, 4 points.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6 covers the south-western edge of Barrington, south of Clement Bridge Road, between Williams Avenue and Shreve Avenue, down to Davis Road, which runs along the bottom of the sheet on the boundary with the Borough of Magnolia. Williams Avenue and Shreve Avenue run the full height of the sheet, Shreve Avenue drawn as a narrow street of about 25 feet, and Centre crosses between them near the top. The land is laid out in long, narrow lots fronting both avenues and the west side of Williams Avenue, numbered as blocks 45, 46 and 46A, with frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories scattered along them, many with sheds, garages and chicken coops behind. A small stream, unnamed, crosses the sheet from left to right just below Centre. East of Shreve Avenue the sheet is open land, block 47 and block 72, with a private road leading to a dwelling and a green house. The area below Davis Road is left blank with a reference to the map of Magnolia, and the word Barrington is lettered near the top. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, turned like sheet 5 so that Williams Avenue runs up the page. The upper right corner of the sheet holds an inset of part of Lawnside, separated by a heavy line, which is a separate part.
notes: Williams Avenue is East Williams Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Centre is Center Street.
Davis Road is drawn on the borough line with Magnolia; the margin reads 'See Map of Magnolia'.

The junction of Davis Road and Shreve Avenue was hand-picked because Shreve Avenue is drawn only about 25 feet wide; both Davis Road points carry residuals of about 2.5 m against a similarity fit, suggesting Davis Road has been widened or straightened since.
Only three street junctions were detected and one hand-picked; low to medium confidence.
100 ft. Part 1: Williams and Shreve Avenues to Davis Road (Magnolia line). Part 2: inset of Lawnside at Mansion or Warwick Avenue, Charleston to Davis Road (Charman Avenue), north up.

sheet-6-2.description: This inset in the upper right corner of sheet 6, set off by a heavy line, shows a small piece of Lawnside around Mansion Avenue, also lettered Warwick, between Charleston Avenue at the top and Davis Road at the bottom, where the borough line with Magnolia runs along the road. Hodges Avenue crosses Mansion Avenue with an offset, so that its eastern half lies further south than its western half, and Charleston Avenue is similarly offset. The blocks, numbered 78 to 84, hold frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories and sheds. Notable buildings are the Lawnside fire company house on Mansion Avenue near Hodges Avenue, a concrete block auto and storage building on Hodges Avenue, and the Grace Temple Baptist Church in the upper right corner. The word Lawnside is lettered across block 79. The area below Davis Road is left blank with a reference to the map of Magnolia, and the borough line is drawn along Davis Road. The inset is drawn at about 100 feet to an inch with north nearly straight up, at a different rotation from the main part of the sheet, and it lies about a kilometre east of it on the ground, east of White Horse Pike.
notes: Mansion Avenue or Warwick is Warwick Road (Warwick Road South north of the Magnolia line) in OpenStreetMap.
Davis Road east of White Horse Pike is Charman Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Charleston Avenue and Hodges Avenue are East and West Charleston Avenue and East and West Hodges Avenue.
Placed by two detected junctions along Warwick Road only (helmert); low confidence.
100 ft. Part 1: Williams and Shreve Avenues to Davis Road (Magnolia line). Part 2: inset of Lawnside at Mansion or Warwick Avenue, Charleston to Davis Road (Charman Avenue), north up.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the part of Barrington east of the railroad, along White Horse Pike, from Clement Bridge Road, also lettered Highland Avenue, at the top down to Bell Avenue at the bottom. Clement Bridge Road runs diagonally across the top of the sheet on the boundary with the Borough of Haddon Heights, whose side is left blank with a reference to the map of Haddon Heights; Chesterfield Road leaves it towards the upper right. At the left edge Atlantic Avenue and Page Avenue run beside the railroad, the Atlantic City Railroad (Philadelphia and Reading Railway), with a row of small lots and frame dwellings in block 51. White Horse Pike runs down the middle of the sheet; the North Branch of Timber Creek crosses it near the top. Below a private road, Wood Avenue, Olive Avenue and Bell Avenue run east from White Horse Pike, with Baptiste Avenue crossing them; the blocks east of Baptiste Avenue, 54A and 57, are divided into narrow lots that are still largely empty. The sheet shows frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories, sheds and chicken coops, with commercial buildings along White Horse Pike and Clement Bridge Road: filling stations with gasoline tanks at the junction of the two roads, stores at Clement Bridge Road near the railroad, an auto service building, a lumber shed and an autos and storage building west of the Pike. Block 54 holds a farmstead with a windmill and water tank on a steel tower and green houses, one marked not used. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the bottom edge continues on sheet 8.
notes: Clement Bridge Road is Clements Bridge Road in OpenStreetMap; Atlantic Avenue is East Atlantic Avenue; the street south of block 51 is East Haines Avenue.
Wood Avenue and Olive Avenue have no counterpart of that name in OpenStreetMap; Copley Road partly follows their line.

The junction of Atlantic Avenue and Haines Avenue was excluded: the detector placed it about 40 ft east of the drawn junction because Atlantic Avenue has only one side drawn beside the railroad. A hand-picked Page Avenue and Haines Avenue point disagreed by 6 m with the other control and was left out.
The margin reads 'See Map of Haddon Heights'.

100 ft. East of the railroad: Clement Bridge Road to Bell Avenue along White Horse Pike; Atlantic and Page Avenues, Wood and Olive Avenues (not in OSM), Baptiste Avenue. One part. second_pass keep: the second pass dropped Bell Avenue / White Horse Pike and moved it 3.2 m away from sheet 8.

sheet-8-1.description: The main part of sheet 8 south of Mouldy Road covers the centre of Lawnside between White Horse Pike on the left and Mansion Avenue or Warwick on the right, down to Elizabeth Avenue and Mott at the bottom. Emlen Avenue crosses the part from White Horse Pike to Mansion Avenue and beyond, and Thomas Avenue and Bryant Avenue run south from Mouldy Road across it to Elizabeth Avenue. East of Mansion Avenue, Church, Emlen Avenue, Phinx Avenue and Mott lead off the edge of the sheet. The blocks, numbered 60 to 70 and 75, are divided into narrow lots built with frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories, sheds and chicken coops, with large empty areas in blocks 62, 67 and 68. Buildings of note are the Mt. Pisgah A.M.E. Church at Mouldy Road and Mansion Avenue, an I.O.O.F. hall, a post office and a lodge hall on Mansion Avenue, the Lawnside Inn on White Horse Pike near Gloucester Pike, an auto repair shop with gasoline tanks at White Horse Pike and Mouldy Road, and a few stores. Block 71, between White Horse Pike and the heavy dividing line on the left, holds a row of dwellings along the Pike. Gloucester Pike leaves White Horse Pike in the lower left corner. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The part of the main map north of Mouldy Road, the strip left of the heavy line and the inset at the upper right are separate parts.
notes: Mansion Avenue or Warwick is Warwick Road North in OpenStreetMap; Phinx Avenue is East and West Phoenix Avenue; Mott is Mott Street; Thomas Avenue is Thomas Avenue North and South either side of Emlen Avenue; Emlen Avenue is East and West Emlen Avenue.
Church has no counterpart of that name in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The junctions of Gloucester Pike with White Horse Pike and of Mouldy Road with Mansion Avenue carried residuals of 4.6 m and 4.7 m and were excluded.

The main map of sheet 8 was split at Mouldy Road: placed as one part, its northern half lay up to about 25 m from where sheet 7 places the shared borough-line mark, because the sheet draws White Horse Pike between Mouldy Road and Bell Avenue about 6 percent short and turned about 4 degrees.

100 ft. Lawnside. Part 1: main map south of Mouldy Road, White Horse Pike to Mansion or Warwick Avenue, Emlen to Elizabeth Avenue and Mott. Part 2: strip west of a heavy line along the west side of White Horse Pike, Gloucester Pike to Davis Road. Part 3: inset top right, Warwick Road from Mott to Gloucester Avenue (London, Brown), Lawnside Public School. Part 4: main map north of Mouldy Road (Mt. Peace Cemetery), split off because the sheet draws it about 6 percent short and turned about 4 degrees; placed from a mark carried from sheet 7.

sheet-8-2.description: This narrow strip along the left edge of sheet 8, set off by a heavy line, shows the west side of White Horse Pike in Lawnside south of the main part of the sheet, from Gloucester Pike at the top down to Davis Road at the bottom, where the borough line between Barrington and Magnolia is drawn along Davis Road and then down the middle of the Pike. The Pike is drawn with its full width of 66 feet at the top, but the dividing line cuts into it further down. West of the Pike the strip shows a row of lots with frame dwellings, sheds and concrete chicken coops, a store with gasoline tanks near Gloucester Pike, and the Mt. Zion M.E. Church (Colored), a stone basement building heated by hot air and lit by electricity, beside block 74, which is lettered Cemetery. The word Lawnside is lettered across the lower part of the strip. The strip is drawn at 100 feet to an inch at the same rotation as the main part of the sheet, but it continues the Pike south of where the main part ends, so it lies several hundred metres from it on the ground.
notes: Placed from a single hand-picked point (Davis Road and White Horse Pike, at the corner of the borough line) with the atlas scale and the rotation of the main part of the sheet; low confidence, especially at the Gloucester Pike end.
Davis Road is drawn on the Barrington and Magnolia borough line.

100 ft. Lawnside. Part 1: main map south of Mouldy Road, White Horse Pike to Mansion or Warwick Avenue, Emlen to Elizabeth Avenue and Mott. Part 2: strip west of a heavy line along the west side of White Horse Pike, Gloucester Pike to Davis Road. Part 3: inset top right, Warwick Road from Mott to Gloucester Avenue (London, Brown), Lawnside Public School. Part 4: main map north of Mouldy Road (Mt. Peace Cemetery), split off because the sheet draws it about 6 percent short and turned about 4 degrees; placed from a mark carried from sheet 7.

sheet-8-3.description: This inset in the upper right corner of sheet 8, set off by a heavy line, continues Lawnside south of the main part of the sheet along Mansion Avenue or Warwick Avenue, from Mott at the top past London and Brown to Gloucester Avenue. London and Brown run east from Mansion Avenue through blocks 76 and 77, which are divided into narrow lots with frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories and sheds; Gloucester Avenue is drawn as a short street on the west side of Mansion Avenue, with block 78 below it. The largest building is the Lawnside Public School in block 82, east of Mansion Avenue, heated by steam and lit by electricity. A small store stands near Mansion Avenue at the top of the inset, and the word Lawnside is lettered across block 82. The inset has its own north arrow pointing nearly straight up, so it is drawn at a different rotation from the main part of the sheet, at about 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Mansion Avenue or Warwick Avenue is Warwick Road North in OpenStreetMap; Brown is Brown Street; London has no counterpart of that name in the OpenStreetMap extract.

Placed by a helmert fit to three points along Warwick Road: Gloucester Avenue (detected) and Brown (hand-picked), and Mott, whose junction with Mansion Avenue lies just outside the inset border and was extrapolated from the two drawn centrelines; the fitted rotation (about 20 degrees) differs from the inset's north arrow (about 12 degrees). Low confidence.

100 ft. Lawnside. Part 1: main map south of Mouldy Road, White Horse Pike to Mansion or Warwick Avenue, Emlen to Elizabeth Avenue and Mott. Part 2: strip west of a heavy line along the west side of White Horse Pike, Gloucester Pike to Davis Road. Part 3: inset top right, Warwick Road from Mott to Gloucester Avenue (London, Brown), Lawnside Public School. Part 4: main map north of Mouldy Road (Mt. Peace Cemetery), split off because the sheet draws it about 6 percent short and turned about 4 degrees; placed from a mark carried from sheet 7.

sheet-8-4.description: The northern part of the main map of sheet 8 covers the area of Lawnside between White Horse Pike and Mansion Avenue or Warwick north of Mouldy Road, up to the borough limits of Barrington and Lawnside and the lots along Bell Avenue at the top of the sheet. Most of it is the open ground of Mt. Peace Cemetery (blocks 58 and 59) and the large empty block 62, with the dash-dot borough line drawn across the cemetery and lettered Barrington and Lawnside. A narrow block west of White Horse Pike, block 71, holds a few frame dwellings and sheds, and along the top a row of narrow lots, block (3), lies south of Bell Avenue. Scattered dwellings, sheds and a small concrete block building stand in block 62 near Mouldy Road, and the word Lawnside is lettered across the middle. A match mark A on White Horse Pike at the top ties the sheet to the bottom of sheet 7. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Separated from the main map of sheet 8 at Mouldy Road because the sheet draws this area about 6 percent short and turned about 4 degrees against the part south of the road.

Placed by three points: the borough-line mark A at White Horse Pike carried from sheet 7, and the junctions of Mouldy Road with Thomas Avenue and Bryant Avenue at their positions detected in the whole-sheet run. With three points the affine fit is exact and has no check; low confidence. A hand-picked Mouldy Road and White Horse Pike point disagreed by about 11 m and was left out.

The mask stops at the dash-dot match line with sheet 7; the lots south of Bell Avenue above it are shown by sheet 7. Below that line the two sheets still disagree: the match marks A and B are about 381 m apart on sheet 7 and 429 m on sheet 8, so the lots along the top of this part lie up to about 30 m from sheet 7's rendering of the same row.

100 ft. Lawnside. Part 1: main map south of Mouldy Road, White Horse Pike to Mansion or Warwick Avenue, Emlen to Elizabeth Avenue and Mott. Part 2: strip west of a heavy line along the west side of White Horse Pike, Gloucester Pike to Davis Road. Part 3: inset top right, Warwick Road from Mott to Gloucester Avenue (London, Brown), Lawnside Public School. Part 4: main map north of Mouldy Road (Mt. Peace Cemetery), split off because the sheet draws it about 6 percent short and turned about 4 degrees; placed from a mark carried from sheet 7.
